```{r}
library(latex2exp)
library(cowplot)
library(gridExtra)

#Take care of the legend

# Exemple simulé si tu n’as pas défini `simul_data`
set.seed(123)
simul_data <- data.frame(
  x = rnorm(100),
  y = rnorm(100),
  `Confidence.Bands` = rep(c("90%", "68%"), each = 50)
  ,
  `Linetype` = rep(c("Main Estimate", "Bootstrap Median"), 50)
)

names <- c("Pelec", "Qelec", "IPI", "CPI", "Policy rate")
# Définir le mapping manuel pour les types de traits
linetype <- c("Bootstrap Median"= "dashed", "Main Estimate" = "solid")

# Plot avec légende uniquement
plot_legend <- ggplot(data = simul_data, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = `Confidence.Bands`), bins = 30, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y, linetype = `Linetype`)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("90%" = "blue", "68%" = "lightblue"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = linetype,
    name = "Linetype",
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal"
  )

# Extraire la légende personnalisée
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
#custom_legend <- get_plot_component(plot_legend, "guide-box", return_all = TRUE)[[3]]

#custom_legend[[3]]
#custom_legend
```



Supply ordonner en premier

```{r}

plot_irf <- function(i, shock, elas_key, results, lambda_0_log, irhor) {

  IRF_50 <- results[[elas_key]]$IRF_50
  IRF_68 <- results[[elas_key]]$IRF_68
  IRF_90 <- results[[elas_key]]$IRF_90

  main_IV <- results[[elas_key]]$lambda_0[, i, shock]

  time_horizon <- 1:irhor

  ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(aes(
      x = time_horizon,
      ymin = IRF_90[1, , i, shock],
      ymax = IRF_90[2, , i, shock]
    ), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(
      x = time_horizon,
      ymin = IRF_68[1, , i, shock],
      ymax = IRF_68[2, , i, shock]
    ), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = main_IV),
              color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = IRF_50[, i, shock]),
              color = "darkblue", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    labs(
      title = names[i],
      # subtitle = paste0("Elasticity = ", elas_key),
      x = "Time",
      y = "Unit Points"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
}


```




```{r}
plot_grid_for_elas <- function(elas_key, shock, results, lambda_0_log, irhor, n) {

  plots <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    plot_irf(
      i = i,
      shock = shock,
      elas_key = elas_key,
      results = results,
      lambda_0_log = lambda_0_log,
      irhor = irhor
    )
  })
    
  grid.arrange(grobs = plots, nrow = 2)
```

```{r}

shock_order <- c(1, 2)  # 1 = Supply, 2 = Demand
shock_names <- c("Supply", "Demand")

elas_grid_demand <- seq(from = -1, to = 0, by = 0.1)
elas_grid_supply <- seq(from = -1, to = 5, by = 0.5)


results_by_elas <- lapply(elas_grid_demand, run_bootstrap_for_elas)
names(results_by_elas) <- paste0( elas_grid_demand)

###### Imppose Supply elas instead of Demand elas
results_by_elas_bis <- lapply(elas_grid_supply, run_bootstrap_for_elas_bis)
names(results_by_elas_bis) <- paste0(elas_grid_supply)


```


```{r}
for (e in elas_grid_demand) {

  elas_key <- paste0(e)

  cat("\n\n")
  cat("## Elasticity =", e, "\n\n")

  for (s in shock_order) {

    cat("### ", shock_names[s], " shock\n\n")

    grid <- plot_grid_for_elas(
      elas_key = elas_key,
      shock = s,
      results = results_by_elas,
      lambda_0_log = lambda_0_log,
      irhor = irhor,
      n = n
    )

    print(grid)
  }
}

```
